requirements.requirement: Cron job on node1 runs /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15
requirements.summary: Root crontab entry '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' was installed and confirmed via crontab -l for root, and cron.service was verified active so the schedule will actually be triggered.

A manual invocation of the command appended its timestamped output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log, and a second run after the restart appended again while preserving prior content, confirming append-mode retention as configured in the crontab redirection.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 8336c3a1... with cron active and crontab intact; shutdown -r now was issued and the connection dropped (refused) then reconnected with a new boot_id 76b1233e...; post-restart checks show cron.service active, the crontab entry intact, prior log content preserved, and a fresh manual run successfully appending to the log. This is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots showing the same boot-identity change from after-prepare to after-executor.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied: the cron schedule and log retention were correctly configured and directly verified through both manual invocation and a full restart cycle, and the mandatory node-restart protocol shows a clean pre-restart baseline, an actual reboot (boot_id change corroborated by fixed lifecycle snapshots), and confirmed recovery of cron, the crontab entry, and log data afterward.
limitations: The actual 02:15 scheduled firing of the cron job was not observed directly (only manual invocations); this is expected given the task was evaluated same-day and is standard for cron-based tasks.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were limited to installing the crontab entry (required), two manual invocations of the maintenance script (bounded, used to verify write/append behavior and post-restart recovery, no unwanted residue), and one reboot (required by the mandatory restart protocol). No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were observed; the one failed command (cmd-b378120be0694364, checking for a pre-existing log file) was a read-only test with return code reflecting 'file missing', not a state change. Temp file churn between after-prepare and after-executor is expected systemd/timesyncd private-directory regeneration from the reboot, not executor residue. No failed services, package inconsistency, or new listening sockets were introduced.
